season_storylines: Patrick Mahomes is fully cleared for camp after tearing his ACL and LCL last December but Andy Reid hints he may sit the entire preseason, and with KC investing in the run game his passing volume and 6-pt-TD ceiling are no longer set-and-forget.

Seattle enters as the defending Super Bowl champion (hosting New England in the Sept 9 opener) while the Rams, after trading for Myles Garrett, sit as Super Bowl favorite at +550 with a league-high 11.5 win total, making both offenses premium environments for TD-driven scoring.

A massive coaching carousel reshuffles fantasy value: Kevin Stefanski to Atlanta (RB/TE friendly), Todd Monken to Cleveland (featured RB), Mike McCarthy to Pittsburgh, Klint Kubiak to Las Vegas (run/boot-action), Robert Saleh with OC Brian Daboll in Tennessee, and Mike LaFleur in Arizona.

Mike McDaniel landed as Chargers OC and his quick-trigger, RB-heavy passing scheme makes Justin Herbert (still a Charger, trade rumors dead), Ladd McConkey, Omarion Hampton and Oronde Gadsden the offseason's biggest scheme winners.

The RB market got paid this week: Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs signed record extensions and Jonathan Taylor added 2 years and 44 million dollars, cementing three true bell-cow goal-line roles that are gold in non-PPR.

Wide receiver musical chairs creates target vacuums: Stefon Diggs joined Jayden Daniels in Washington, DJ Moore reunited with Joe Brady in Buffalo, Mike Evans signed with San Francisco, and Jaylen Waddle now runs deep routes for Bo Nix in Denver.

Four live QB battles will set streaming value: Kyler Murray is out-repping J.J. McCarthy in Minnesota, Tua Tagovailoa leads a rehabbing Michael Penix Jr. in Atlanta, Deshaun Watson is edging an unimpressive Shedeur Sanders in Cleveland, and Kirk Cousins was named Raiders QB1 over No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza.

San Francisco's pass-catcher room is being wrecked by injuries: Ricky Pearsall is out for the season after PCL surgery, George Kittle (Achilles) could miss 4-plus weeks if not activated from PUP, and Mike Evans (quad) and Christian Kirk (calf) are banged up, funneling early-season value to Jake Tonges and De'Zhaun Stribling.

Malik Nabers is on track to return from his torn ACL for Week 1 with a worst case of missing 1-2 games, stabilizing the Giants passing game for second-year dual-threat Jaxson Dart, who finished QB13 as a rookie.

Miami's teardown is the league's bleakest fantasy landscape: a 4.5 win total (lowest on the board), new HC Jeff Hafley, Malik Willis on a make-or-break deal, and De'Von Achane facing constant negative game scripts.

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur brings McVay-tree motion and TE-heavy sets, but with Jacoby Brissett bridging to rookie Carson Beck and one of the lowest win totals on the board, the fantasy plays are No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love's workload and Marvin Harrison Jr. in the funnel role.

Kevin Stefanski takes over an offense with freshly-extended Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts, and with Tua Tagovailoa set to start while Michael Penix Jr. rehabs his ACL (no preseason expected), the RB and TE are the TD-equity plays.

The Ravens carry a league-high 11.5 win total into a new-look staff under HC Jesse Minter (verify), and with Isaiah Likely gone Mark Andrews profiles as a consolidated red-zone TE1 in an offense built on rushing efficiency.

A 10.5 win total and Josh Allen's rushing TD floor remain elite for 6-pt-TD formats, and DJ Moore's arrival under OC Joe Brady gives the offense a legitimate yardage-and-TD X receiver at a flex price.

Carolina's 7.5 win total reflects a rising roster, but camp has been costly with rookie WR Chris Brazzell and pass rusher Nic Scourton lost for the season, leaving newly-extended slot man Jalen Coker as the sneaky value in a slot role that plays down in non-PPR.
A 9.5 win total and top-5 power ranking say the Ben Johnson offense has arrived, and DJ Moore's exit vacates targets that make Luther Burden III the clear ascending yardage-and-TD play.
A 10.5 win total keeps this a premium passing environment, with camp buzz pointing to Chase Brown's stock rising as the lead back and TE Erick All Jr. finally healthy after knee procedures (verify).

Todd Monken's featured-RB scheme makes Quinshon Judkins the clear fantasy centerpiece on a 5.5-win team whose QB battle between an INT-prone Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders caps every pass catcher except TE Harold Fannin Jr.

A 9.5 win total and top-10 power ranking suggest a stable, pace-neutral offense where the top passing-game options hold value and Ryan Flournoy opens as the No. 3 WR with injury-contingent upside only.

Denver is a top-3 power-ranking team at a 9.5 win total, and adding deep threat Jaylen Waddle (minor leg strain, back within a week) to back-to-back QB7 Bo Nix raises the whole offense's yardage-per-point ceiling.

Jahmyr Gibbs' record extension locks in a dual-purpose bell cow, and Jared Goff keeps averaging 17-plus PPG while being drafted around QB16, making Detroit's 10.5-win offense a value across the board.

Tucker Kraft is off PUP and trending toward Week 1 after his torn ACL, and a thinner receiver room makes deep threat Christian Watson exactly the kind of low-catch, high-yardage-and-TD breakout non-PPR rewards.
A 9.5 win total and top-6 power ranking keep C.J. Stroud's passing tree valuable, with Jayden Higgins having locked up the No. 2 WR job and Tank Dell's knee still a monitor.

Jonathan Taylor's 2-year 44 million extension confirms the goal-line bell cow, while the Michael Pittman trade opens a career-year target share for Josh Downs, whose slot profile still needs TDs to matter in non-PPR.

Travis Etienne's departure makes explosive rookie-contract back Bhayshul Tuten the favorite for lead touches, though Chris Rodriguez Jr.'s foot injury is worth tracking in a backfield on an 8.5-win offense.

Mahomes is cleared from his ACL/LCL tear but may skip the whole preseason, and a deliberate shift toward the run trims the passing ceiling, downgrading Mahomes and an aging Travis Kelce while healthy speedster Xavier Worthy (shoulder being managed, verify) is the value.

New OC Mike McDaniel's quick-game scheme with 21-plus percent of early-down targets to RBs boosts Justin Herbert's efficiency and makes Omarion Hampton a yardage monster, with Ladd McConkey and Oronde Gadsden the middle-of-field winners.

The Super Bowl favorite at +550 with a league-high 11.5 win total after the Myles Garrett trade, the Rams offer premium TD equity everywhere, with Blake Corum one Kyren Williams injury from league-winning volume and a Melbourne opener vs the 49ers.

Klint Kubiak imports the champion Seahawks' boot-action, 12-personnel run game with Kirk Cousins named QB1 over No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza, setting up Ashton Jeanty for a TD-heavy workhorse leap and Brock Bowers as the seam winner despite a 5.5 win total.

The league's lowest win total at 4.5 under new HC Jeff Hafley with Malik Willis at QB means chronic negative scripts, so De'Von Achane's efficiency-dependent profile is risky and Malik Washington is only a cheap yardage dart as the emerging top receiver.

Kyler Murray is taking the bulk of first-team reps and looks set to beat out J.J. McCarthy (12 INTs in 10 starts last year), and his rushing floor plus Justin Jefferson at a QB17-ish price makes him a prime 6-pt-TD league target.

A 10.5 win total and a playoff win last season mark this offense as ascendant, and 5.1-yards-per-carry TreVeyon Henderson is earning the Year 2 role that non-PPR loves: explosive yardage with goal-line upside.

Tyler Shough flashed late in his rookie year and has added weapons, but rookie WR Brock Rechsteiner's six-game suspension and Bryan Bresee's season-ending injury dent a 7.5-win roster still best treated as a streaming source.

A new staff with OC Matt Nagy leaning 12/13 personnel supports TE Theo Johnson, and Jaxson Dart's dual-threat game (QB13 as a rookie) plus Malik Nabers on track for Week 1 off his ACL give the 7.5-win Giants real fantasy juice.

Geno Smith was last in the league in passing yards with 17 INTs, making him poison at -2 per pick, and with rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq now expected to miss time with a groin injury the only cheap angles are Mason Taylor and a possible midseason Cade Klubnik pivot on a 5.5-win team.

New OC Sean Mannion adds motion and play-action that helps DeVonta Smith and rookie Makai Lemon (positioned as the No. 2, verify), but Jalen Hurts' rushing volume fell to 105 carries with goal-line work going to committee, cutting into the exact TD equity that made him elite.

Mike McCarthy takes over with public friction after Aaron Rodgers criticized the team this week, so the safer plays on the 8.5-win Steelers are the DK Metcalf yardage role and a Jaylen Warren/Rico Dowdle backfield with real TD share.

The defending champs carry a 10.5 win total and the No. 2 power ranking into a Sept 9 opener vs New England, and with Kenneth Walker gone and Zach Charbonnet on PUP with a knee issue, Jadarian Price opens camp as the lead back in a title-winning run game.

A 9.5-win contender whose receiving corps is decimated (Pearsall out for the year, Kittle's Achilles could cost 4-plus weeks, Evans and Kirk banged up), pushing early value to Jake Tonges and De'Zhaun Stribling while age-30 Christian McCaffrey carries 400-plus-touch regression risk.

Baker Mayfield enters a contract year feeling disrespected after his worst season as a starter and Vita Vea wants a trade, but Mike Evans' departure hands Emeka Egbuka the alpha red-zone role that matters most in non-PPR.

Robert Saleh hands the offense to Brian Daboll, whose system has produced top-10 QB seasons, making Year 2 Cam Ward the intriguing 6-pt-TD flier with Elic Ayomanor outside and TE Gunnar Helm inheriting 79 vacated targets.

Stefon Diggs signing to play with Jayden Daniels adds a proven target earner to a 7.5-win offense whose QB rushing floor is the fantasy engine, while Rachaad White is a cheap bet on backfield touches (verify role split).

breakout_watch.name: Quinshon Judkins
breakout_watch.why: Todd Monken has a long history of featured-RB usage and Judkins already showed starter chops; a goal-line-inclusive workload on a run-first Browns team is exactly what non-PPR pays for.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Finished RB11 as a rookie and now gets Klint Kubiak's boot-action run scheme imported from the champion Seahawks; volume plus TD equity with no catch-volume dependency.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel's scheme has produced consecutive top-5 RB finishes and funnels 21-plus percent of early-down passes to backs; Hampton gets yardage, TDs, and cheap receiving yards on top.

breakout_watch.name: TreVeyon Henderson
breakout_watch.why: 5.1 yards per carry and a growing Year 2 role in a 10.5-win Patriots offense; explosive per-touch yardage is the non-PPR cheat code.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Favorite to lead the Jaguars backfield after Travis Etienne's departure, and his big-play rushing profile converts directly at 10 yards per point.

breakout_watch.name: Jadarian Price
breakout_watch.why: Opens camp as the top back in the defending champs' run game with Kenneth Walker gone and Zach Charbonnet on PUP; title-team volume plus goal-line looks.

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: Running backs don't go No. 3 overall to sit; even on a bad Cardinals team the projected workload and goal-line monopoly carry a high non-PPR floor.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Mike Evans' departure vacates the alpha X and red-zone role in Tampa; Egbuka already produced as a rookie and inherits the TD tree.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: DJ Moore's exit opens a large target share in Ben Johnson's ascending Bears offense; the yardage-after-catch profile scores even without PPR help.

breakout_watch.name: Christian Watson
breakout_watch.why: Classic non-PPR asymmetry: a field-stretching deep threat in a thinned Packers WR room who wins on yards and TDs, not catch volume.

breakout_watch.name: Jayden Higgins
breakout_watch.why: Locked up the No. 2 job with C.J. Stroud in a 9.5-win offense; a size/red-zone profile at a mid-130s ADP is free TD equity.

breakout_watch.name: Jaxson Dart
breakout_watch.why: QB13 as a rookie with a real rushing component, and Malik Nabers is on track for Week 1; 6-pt passing TDs plus rushing yards make him a top-10 upside pick at a discount.

breakout_watch.name: Kyler Murray
breakout_watch.why: Winning the Vikings job with the bulk of first-team reps, paired with Justin Jefferson; his rushing floor plus 6-pt TDs at a QB17-ish price is the draft's best QB arbitrage.

breakout_watch.name: Bo Nix
breakout_watch.why: Back-to-back QB7-caliber finishes, a rushing floor, and now Jaylen Waddle stretching defenses; low-INT profile is doubly valuable at -2 per pick.

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Age-30 season coming off 400-plus touches; only one back in 13 years has followed that workload with a top-5 finish, and SF's injury-riddled receiving corps invites defenses to load the box.

fade_watch.name: Patrick Mahomes
fade_watch.why: Cleared from the ACL/LCL tear but may not take a preseason snap, and KC's deliberate run-game investment cuts the passing volume that justified his price; pay for the finish, not the name.

fade_watch.name: Travis Kelce
fade_watch.why: Turns 37 with a rehabbing QB and a run-tilted offense; every arrow points down and TE catch volume is worth nothing here without TDs.

fade_watch.name: Jalen Hurts
fade_watch.why: Rushing fell to 105 carries and the goal-line work is moving to committee; his fantasy premium was built on rushing TDs that are no longer guaranteed.

fade_watch.name: De'Von Achane
fade_watch.why: Miami's 4.5-win total means constant trailing scripts, his production leans on big-play efficiency that regresses, and his pass-catching cushion is worth far less in non-PPR.

fade_watch.name: Baker Mayfield
fade_watch.why: Contract-year friction after failed extension talks and his worst statistical season since becoming a starter; the INT risk at -2 apiece makes him a streamer, not a starter.

fade_watch.name: Geno Smith
fade_watch.why: Last in the NFL in passing yards per game with 17 INTs last season; in a -2 INT format on a 5.5-win team he is actively negative, with a rookie lurking behind him.

fade_watch.name: Deshaun Watson
fade_watch.why: Likely wins the Browns job by default but has thrown multiple INTs in half his camp practices coming off an Achilles tear; avoid, and discount every Cleveland pass catcher accordingly.

fade_watch.name: Derrick Henry
fade_watch.why: Age-cliff workload profile flagged across bust lists this summer; the yardage floor is fine but paying an early pick for a declining TD-dependent back is how non-PPR teams die (verify current workload split).

uncertainty_note: Genuinely unsettled right now: the Vikings (Murray vs McCarthy) and Browns (Watson vs Sanders) QB calls are not official; Mahomes' preseason participation and Week 1 sharpness are unknown; George Kittle's PUP activation, Tucker Kraft's Week 1 status, and Malik Nabers' final clearance are all pending; several 2026 roster fits reported here (Eagles No. 2 WR, Ravens coaching staff, Cardinals exact win total, Xavier Worthy's shoulder) come from single-source summaries and are tagged (verify); preseason games this weekend could reshuffle multiple ambiguous backfields.
